full_judgment:
Amirul Kabir Chowdhury J : The State represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka seeks leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 18-7-2004 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9046 of 2002 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The said Rule was heard with Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 8038 and 4275 of 2002 and has been disposed of by the same judgment and order of the High Court Division. Civil Petitions for leave to Appeal Nos. 56 and 57 of 2005 arise out of aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 8038 of 2002 and 4275 of 2002 respectively. Hence this judgment shall govern both the aforesaid petitions too. 

 3. The facts, in short, are that Jalal Uddin Ahmed, Inspector (task force-1) Bureau of Anti-Corruption, Bangladesh, Dhaka lodged a first information report on 11-12-200 I against Mohammad Nasim (respondent in Criminal Petition No. 55 of 2005), Safiur Rahman (respondent in Criminal Petition No. 56 of 2005) and Abdur Razzaque (respondent in Criminal Petition No. 57 of 2005) and others stating, inter alia, that the respondents Mohammad Nasim was Minister-in- Charge of Ministry of Home, Safiur Rahman was Secretary, Ministry of Home and Abdur Razzaque was Chairman, Ace Business Systems Limited during the period of 1999-2000. They being in collusion with each other along with other accused mentioned in the first information report did not give/issue work order to the lowest tenderer Calcutta Security Printers Limited, India for supplying ten lac unwritten passport books and instead issued the work order to the 2nd lowest tenderer Francois Charles Oberthur, France in short FCO and thus obtained pecuniary advantage for themselves and/or others and hence committed offence punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. On the basis of the aforesaid first information report, Ramna Police Station Case No.53 dated 11-12-2001 was started against them. After investigation charge-sheet has been submitted against the accused respondents and others on 2-4-2002. 

 4. The three respondents appeared before the courts below and were released on bail. Thereafter they moved the High Court Division under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding against them. The aforesaid Criminal Miscellaneous Cases were thus started in the High Court Division. The High Court Division after hearing the parties made the Rules absolute and quashed the proceeding of aforesaid Ramna Police Station Case No. 53 dated 11-12- 2001. Hence are these petitions. 

 5. In support of the petitions Mr Faisal H Khan, learned Assistant Attorney-General, submits, inter alia, that on plain reading of the first information report and the charge-sheet strong prima facie case being disclosed the High Court Division committed error in quashing the proceeding. 

 7. Mr Amir-ul Islam, learned Senior Advocate appeared in Criminal Petition No.55 of 2005 and 56 of 2005 and submits that in the comparative statement as has been prepared by the tender committee it was found that the lowest tenderer Calcutta Security Printers Limited, India have no previous experience and they have not printed any passport. On the other hand, the Francois Charles Oberthur, France (FCO), has printed and supplied passports in 27 countries including ICAO approved MRP. Therefore, the 2nd lowest bidder Francois Charles Oberthur, France has been given the work order and on negotiation the rate of printing of passports was reduced from US$ 1.53 to US$ 1.49 and the respondents discharged their routine official duties and hence did not commit any wrong which comes under the mischief of sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. The petitioner Md Nasim being the Minister of the said Ministry approved the same as per noting of the concerned official responsible for the evaluation of the tender and it was done bonafide in usual course of business in accordance with law and in compliance of his lawful duty as a concerned Minister. The petitioner Safiur Rahman was the Secretary of the said Ministry who approved the same as per noting of the concerned officials responsible for the evaluation of the tender and it was done bonafide in usual course of business in accordance with law. Therefore, the respondents did not commit any offence punishable under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. 

 "5. Criminal Misconduct.(1) A public servant is said to commit the offence of criminal misconduct- 

 12. From the aforesaid provision it appears that if any public servant in any way abusing his position as 'public servant, obtains or attempts to obtain for himself or for any other person any valuable thing or pecuniary advantage is said to commit the offence of misconduct punishable under the law. 

 15. We have given our anxious consideration to the facts and circumstances of the case. From the first information report, or charge-sheet it does not appear that the respondents Md Nasim and/or Safiur Rahman obtained or attempted to obtain any pecuniary advantage abusing their position as Minister and Secretary of the Ministry of Home. In the whole deal we do not find any element of mens rea on the part of the respondents inasmuch as their actions appear to be bonafide. 

 16. We are of the view that when the Tender Committee forwarded the matter to the Ministry with, the opinion that the first lowest Tenderer stood disqualified for non-fulfillment of the condition of  the Tender schedule, the Respondents (the Minister or and Secretary) did not commit any offence, agreeing to issue work order to' the second lowest Tenderer, more so, after bargaining the rate being fixed to 1.49 US Dollar in lieu of 1.53 US Dollar quoted by the second lowest tenderer previously. From the first , information report it appears that contents thereof even if accepted in its entirety no prima facie case is disclosed and, as such, we, are of the view that the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in passing the impugned judgment and order quashing the proceeding.
